title: Differential forms, the Poincaré lemma and de Rham cohomology
summary: The exterior algebra of a vector space; differential forms and the exterior derivative with d² = 0 (Theorem 25.1); cochain complexes (Definition 25.3) and de Rham cohomology; the Poincaré lemma and homotopy invariance (§25.2); the beginning of Čech cohomology (§26).

objectives.description: Compute wedge products, pullbacks and exterior derivatives with consistent signs, and prove d²=0 and naturality.
Construct the homotopy operator, prove the Poincaré lemma on a star-shaped domain, and deduce homotopy invariance.
Distinguish local exactness from global exactness by computing periods and the first de Rham cohomology of a punctured plane.

preparation.description: Read lecture 31: §25 the exterior algebra, differential forms, Theorem 25.1 (d² = 0), Definition 25.3 (cochain complex).
Read lecture 32: §25.2 the Poincaré lemma and homotopy invariance of de Rham cohomology; §26 Čech cohomology (first part).
Read Hitchin §5–5.1 (tensor products, exterior algebra), §6.1 (bundle of p-forms), §6.4 (exterior derivative) and §6.6 (de Rham cohomology) for the fuller treatment.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Every closed form is exact because d²=0.
commonMisconceptions.correction: The identity only proves exact forms are closed. Poincaré gives a local converse; a nonzero period obstructs a global primitive.

commonMisconceptions.claim: A two-form always wedges with itself to zero.
commonMisconceptions.correction: The sign rule forces this for odd degree over the reals. An even-degree form can have a nonzero square.
